description: Authorised file-specific new historical image original download batch for gaps in 44 chapter audit

items.title: Surveying and sketching in Porirua Bush in the 1840s
items.credit: Samuel Charles Brees (1810–1865); Alexander Turnbull Library historical image
items.caption: Samuel Charles Brees with a theodolite, sketchbook and fellow surveyors in Porirua Bush, with a vignette of the Hutt River below.
items.context: The published illustration shows the observations and field measurements that preceded electronic survey calculation. It is historical surveying, not digital computation.
items.altText: Historical engraved scene showing nineteenth-century surveyors, a theodolite, sketchbook and a Wellington-area riverscape.

items.commonsTitle: File:Surveyors and theodolite on Tripp Station.jpg
items.title: Surveyors using a theodolite at Tripp Station
items.dateDisplay: date not established on cited Commons file
items.credit: Archives New Zealand, R21011360, AAQT 6539 W3537 28/A47; photographer unidentified
items.caption: Historical photograph of surveyors working with a theodolite at Tripp Station, from an Archives New Zealand publicity collection.
items.context: The original photograph demonstrates the field surveying observations from which bearings and coordinates were calculated. The original capture year requires archive confirmation.
items.altText: Archival photograph of surveyors and a theodolite operating on Tripp Station.

items.commonsTitle: File:1909 Map of Petone and Lower Hutt NZMS013 WN82.jpg
items.title: Petone and Lower Hutt survey map with trig stations, 1909
items.credit: J. W. Davis, Chief Draughtsman, New Zealand Department of Lands and Survey
items.caption: 1909 Department of Lands and Survey map of Petone and Lower Hutt with triangulation stations, survey districts and urban streets.
items.context: Specific historical example of the trig controls and spatial records that were used before electronic coordinate computation. It does not depict a 1960s computer.
items.altText: Detailed 1909 survey map of Petone and Lower Hutt showing trig stations, streets and boundaries.

items.commonsTitle: File:Map of Survey Districts Clutha and South Molyneux (1955).jpg
items.title: Clutha and South Molyneux survey district maps, 1955
items.credit: Department of Lands and Survey; Archives New Zealand DABB D101 409/16 (R6619077)
items.caption: NZMS 13 cadastral survey district sheets covering Clutha and South Molyneux, 1:63,360, third edition, 1955.
items.context: This printed survey map is a pre-computer reference for the later development of automated cartography. It must not be described as plotter-generated.
items.altText: Two detailed cadastral survey district maps with parcel divisions, contours and printed marginal information.

items.commonsTitle: File:1988 aerial image of Verdon College site.jpg
items.title: Historical aerial photography of Verdon College, Invercargill, 1988
items.credit: Southland Regional Council; sourced from LINZ Data Service
items.caption: 1988 aerial survey image showing the site of Verdon College in Invercargill, cropped by the publisher for reference.
items.context: An identifiable historical aerial survey frame from the pre-digital era that illustrates photographic material later incorporated into GIS. It was captured in 1988, after the first 1970s remote-sensing experiments.
items.altText: Aerial survey image of the Verdon College site in Invercargill, captured in 1988.

items.title: Wilding pines beside State Highway 80, Canterbury
items.dateDisplay: date not stated in Commons extracted metadata
items.caption: Wilding conifers viewed westwards towards the Southern Alps from the junction of State Highways 8 and 80 in Canterbury.
items.context: A documented New Zealand forestry-management landscape illustrating one subject of GIS-based land-cover inventories and control planning. The photograph itself is not a GIS map.
items.altText: Wilding pine trees growing across dry Canterbury high-country land beside the State Highway 80 junction.

items.title: Ruapehu Crater Lake theodolite observations, 1988
items.credit: Don Swanson, United States Geological Survey; subject Brad Scott, New Zealand Geological Survey
items.caption: New Zealand Geological Survey volcanologist Brad Scott using a theodolite near Ruapehu Crater Lake in 1988 to monitor volcanic activity.
items.context: A documented scientific observation connected to recurrent volcano-monitoring measurements later assembled with lake chemistry and seismic data. It is a photographic field measurement, not a GIS screenshot.
items.altText: Volcanologist Brad Scott making theodolite observations at Ruapehu Crater Lake in 1988.

items.title: LINZ Topo50 topographic map of Ongaonga, 2020
items.credit: Land Information New Zealand; Topo50 sheet BL37 Ongaonga
items.caption: Section of the LINZ Topo50 map for Ongaonga, derived from sheet BL37, showing modern topographic cartography.
items.context: An actual LINZ digital-era topographic product useful for comparison with the paper NZMS series. The image represents 2020 mapping, not the initial NZMS260 conversion in 1977.
items.altText: Colour LINZ Topo50 map showing Ongaonga and surrounding roads, contours and features.

items.title: Road hierarchy and routes across the Auckland region
items.dateDisplay: publication date to confirm at source
items.credit: Shaundd; OpenStreetMap-derived mapping with LINZ base information where attributed on Commons
items.caption: Map of the Auckland region at approximately 1:900,000, with motorways, state highways and other roads separately symbolised.
items.context: A named contemporary cartographic example of roads as networked spatial data. It does not establish when road-centreline or property datasets were digitised.
items.altText: Regional map of Auckland showing cities, motorways, state highways and secondary roads.

items.title: Geodetic survey mark outside The Riverhead, Auckland
items.caption: Photograph of a physical geodetic survey mark outside The Riverhead building in Riverhead, Auckland, in February 2025.
items.context: Illustrates the visible survey marks used to relate measured positions to geodetic reference frameworks. The mark's actual NZGD2000 status has not been checked and must not be asserted.
items.altText: Close photograph of a geodetic survey mark near The Riverhead building in Auckland.

items.title: New Zealand passenger rail services shown as a national network
items.dateDisplay: source map publication date not established
items.credit: Jkan997; KiwiRail service information on a CC BY-SA map
items.caption: National map of KiwiRail passenger routes including Northern Explorer, Capital Connection, Coastal Pacific and TranzAlpine services.
items.context: An actual transport-network map showing edges and connections, useful as a network-cartography example. It is not a water or electricity utility map, nor an original enterprise GIS screen.
items.altText: New Zealand passenger rail map with distinct lines representing Northern Explorer, Capital Connection, Coastal Pacific and TranzAlpine services.

items.commonsTitle: File:Tsunami forecast map New Zealand 5 March 2021.jpg
items.title: NEMA tsunami forecast following the March 2021 Kermadec earthquakes
items.caption: Official tsunami forecast map issued on 5 March 2021 following large earthquakes near the Kermadec Islands.
items.context: An identifiable emergency-management map product that demonstrates geographic information used for public safety communication. It relates to disaster warnings, rather than police operational mapping.
items.altText: National Emergency Management Agency map showing forecast tsunami effects around New Zealand in March 2021.

items.commonsTitle: File:Survey of Earthquake Fault Trace map - Masterton Earthquake (June 24 1942) (18749413649).jpg
items.title: Survey of fault traces following the Masterton earthquake, 1942
items.dateDisplay: 24 June 1942 event; survey document date to verify
items.credit: Archives New Zealand; original surveyor not identified
items.caption: Historical map recording fault traces associated with the 24 June 1942 Masterton earthquake.
items.context: An original pre-GIS disaster/geological survey illustration. It demonstrates mapped earthquake evidence before electronic and real-time mapping; it must not be labelled a live GIS map.
items.altText: 1942 historical fault-trace survey map showing plotted faults following the Wairarapa earthquake.

items.title: New River Hundred cadastral survey map, 1898
items.credit: W. Deverell; Department of Lands and Survey; Archives New Zealand DABB D101 423/IN 38 (R6617598)
items.caption: Map of New River Hundred, 1898, one of a set of cadastral maps produced by the Department of Lands and Survey.
items.context: A surviving example of printed cadastral cartography documenting land parcels long before nationwide digital cadastral databases.
items.altText: Nineteenth-century New Zealand cadastral map of New River Hundred with survey parcel boundaries and markings.

items.title: NASA mapping of the 2009 Fiordland earthquake
items.credit: NASA Earth Observatory, Jesse Allen; USGS seismic data; SRTM elevation and ocean-bathymetry sources
items.caption: NASA/USGS map of the July 2009 Fiordland earthquake, combining its epicentre, topography and plate-boundary context.
items.context: A specific analytical earthquake map created from seismic and elevation datasets, representing a published product rather than a real-time operations display.
items.altText: NASA topographic map showing the earthquake epicentre off southwest Fiordland in July 2009.
